headline: 📥 THE OFFER LANDED AT 2:20 THIS AFTERNOON — 225 WILLOW POINT IS OFFICIALLY IN NEGOTIATION, AND THE HOUSE IS NO LONGER THE PROBLEM. Molly G. emailed the full packet at 2:20:39 and texted ninety seconds later: purchase agreement already BUYER-SIGNED, personal-property addendum, FHA addendum, and a pre-approval letter written to $185,000. ⭐ SEVEN DAYS, FOUR TOURS, THREE BROKERAGES, AND NOT ONE AGENT EVER ARGUED THE PRICE — that is what a correctly priced listing looks like once the marketing finds the buyers. 🔴 BUT TWO THINGS ARE OWED TONIGHT AND BOTH ARE YOURS: she asked in writing to be told the offer was received and there is still no reply to her, and at 2:51 you told her flood insurance runs about $70 a month when your own sellers’ escrow statement says roughly $1,800 a year — more than double — on an FHA file where flood is escrowed and underwritten. · DO: acknowledge Molly’s offer and correct the flood number · DECIDE: three frozen leads need your 30-second ruling before tomorrow · WATCH: the flood quote is contradicted by two of your own receipts (sellers 8/23, your confirmation 8/24).

notes: ✅ THE FLEET RAN CLEAN THROUGH A DAY THAT ACTUALLY HAD SOMETHING TO CATCH. Roughly forty routine runs since yesterday evening — the money pulse, the trading cockpit, the letter, the marketing machine, the market-report lane, the milestone engine, the listing amplifier and about twenty ISA sweeps — and every one of them reported in. 🔍 ONE BLOCKED LINE APPEARED IN THE WINDOW AND IT HAS ALREADY CLOSED ITSELF: the 8:47 a.m. deep sweep could not import from the Brivity opportunities source because that source carries no email addresses at all; the 4:45 p.m. run of the same routine imported one successfully. Disclosed rather than buried — this board reads OK because the block is closed, not because nobody checked.

📥 THE AFTERNOON DELIVERED THE THING THE MORNING BOARD WAS WAITING ON. At 12:45 this board reported that the promised Willow Point offer had not arrived and its clock had expired; it arrived at 2:20 with the buyer’s signature already on it. ⭐ THE MILESTONE ENGINE CAUGHT IT ON ITS OWN AT 5:05 AND ADVANCED THE LISTING TO OFFER RECEIVED — and it did something better than that: it refused to print an offer price, because the number lives inside a PDF attachment and nothing in this fleet can open one. The $185,000 on the pre-approval is the buyer’s ceiling, not their offer. 🎉 198 Rena also went from signature to open escrow today — contract-to-close details out at 11:34, the title office answered in six minutes.

⚠️ THE ONE THING THE MACHINE FOUND THAT NOBODY WAS LOOKING FOR IS A NUMBER CONTRADICTION ON A LIVE FHA DEAL. Your 2:51 text to the buyer’s agent quoted flood insurance at roughly $70 a month; your sellers gave you roughly $1,800 a year on 8/23 and you confirmed that same figure back to them on 8/24. 🔍 THAT IS TWO OF YOUR OWN RECEIPTS AGAINST ONE TEXT, on the exact line item an FHA underwriter escrows. Your teammate independently asked at 4:32 whether the buyers knew about the flood, and that question has not been answered either. 📉 Elsewhere the day was quietly good: your drafts folder fell from 16 at midday to 11 tonight because you kept working it by hand, and the lead lanes proved themselves dry on every sweep rather than assuming it.

🔴 THE MOST EXPENSIVE LISTING IN THE BOOK AND NOT ONE TOUR HAS EVER BEEN BOOKED ON IT, day 34. ⭐ TODAY SHARPENED THE POINT RATHER THAN SOFTENING IT: a $185,000 listing took four tours and a signed offer in seven days off the same marketing machine that has never produced a single booking here. 🔍 The comp work says the big-house ceiling in that zip is roughly $950K unless acreage carries it — which makes the silence a pricing answer, not a marketing one. 📞 A handoff call is also still owed on this address to the agent who passed it to you.

Re-cut it before you forecast off it again. No fresh pipeline letter this week; team pace sits at 35 against 90, with listings taken at 36 of 54.
